_comment: stats-window.json - which days a statistics period covers.
Loaded by BOTH suites:
Android  app/src/test/kotlin/.../domain/StatsWindowVectorTest.kt
iOS      ios/PotillusKit/Tests/PotillusKitTests/StatsWindowTests.swift
The arithmetic is duplicated by necessity - java.time on one side,
Foundation Calendar on the other - so every boundary below is a place the
two could drift apart: the day a month begins, the day the previous period
ends, the leap day, and the user's statistics-start floor.
Until the 0.84.0 review these cases existed only as Swift unit tests, and
the Kotlin derivation sat inline in StatsViewModel where a JVM test could
not reach it. The expected values were computed independently of both
implementations, not read back from either.
hasBaseline is previousFrom <= previousTo. False means there is no
comparable history, NOT that the baseline was zero grams - a distinction
the floor cases below exist to pin.
The floor is compared as a STRING on both platforms, which works only
because yyyy-MM-dd sorts chronologically.
invalidToday holds only inputs BOTH platforms unambiguously reject. A
invalidToday covers three ways a date can fail: not a date at all, a day the
calendar does not have, and a spelling that is not canonical. Both platforms
reject all three - Kotlin because LocalDate.parse throws, iOS because
DayResolver.parseDate formats its result back and demands the original string
rather than resting on DateFormatter's leniency.

window.description: The week is a rolling window of seven days ending today
The month runs from the first and compares against the whole previous month
The year runs from January first
On the first of a month the period is a single day
The leap day is included in the previous month
On January first the year is one day and the previous is whole
A 31-day previous month keeps all 31 days
A week window spans a year boundary

invalidToday.description: A malformed date yields no window
An empty date yields no window
A day the calendar does not have yields no window
A non-canonical spelling yields no window

adjacency._comment: previousTo is always the day before from, for every period and day.

applyingFloor.description: A floor before both windows changes nothing
A floor inside the previous period shortens the baseline
A floor inside the current period leaves no baseline
The floor is applied by string comparison
A floor on the current period's first day leaves the current window untouched but still removes the baseline
